policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 5 May close (1x4 3.88, 3x6 4.06, 6x9 4.43, 9x12 4.62 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 75bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 9 Apr; the 5-6 May meeting is expected to hold. Dąbrowski (30 Apr): the chance of cuts fell sharply after the April CPI. April flash CPI 3.2% (30 Apr; 3.0% expected); core 2.7% in March. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 May.
policy.risk_text: Hawkish drift: April CPI 3.2% with core rising, FRAs price ~70bp of hikes while the MPC talks hold, and May supply is heavy (PLN 19-37bn) with Brent above $100; a US-Iran deal is the relief valve.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); the fiscal notification and the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) to 15 May.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~49% (after 28 Apr, MoF) financed; budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April (MoF estimate). S&P reviews Poland on 8 May (A-, stable; Erste sees a sizeable risk of a negative outlook); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP has held at 3.75% since the 4 Mar cut (next MPC 5-6 May); April CPI 3.2% y/y; 2025 GDP 3.6%, Q4 4.1%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 5 May: the MPC began its two-day meeting; POLGB yields edged up (10Y ~5.78%, near a one-month high, ING) ahead of a possibly hawkish Glapiński and heavy May supply; PKO: the market prices a 25bp NBP hike in 2026 and another 50bp in 2027, ING calls the hike pricing too aggressive; the EC received Poland's SAFE loan agreement. Abroad: the US said the ceasefire holds and ships crossed Hormuz; Brent ~$111; gilt 10Y 5.1% (2008 high) with nearly three BoE hikes and more than three ECB hikes priced; Romania's government fell and the leu hit a record low.

calendar.plan_text: MoF May plan (30 Apr): sale auctions on 13 May (PLN 6-12bn), 21 May (7-13bn) and 27 May (6-12bn) in OK0129 (new 2Y, replaces OK0128), NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; a 46-week T-bill on 8 May (3-6bn); no switch. ~49% of 2026 needs financed after the April sales.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining May sales: 13 May, 21 May, 27 May. MPC 5-6 May: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: oil shock with a stalled US-Iran truce (Brent above $100, Bund near 2011 highs) and hawkish repricing abroad; the NBP is at 3.75% while FRAs price roughly 75bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the BoE for hikes, the Fed has turned to hike risk, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 52bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 276bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 5 May close). Gilt 10Y 5.1%, a 2008 high; Romania's government falls (5 May).

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).
Supply: BGK sold PLN 0.69bn on 29 Apr plus 0.13bn additional (demand 0.94bn); next FPC tenders 14 and 28 May; the FWSZ 2026 bond plan was raised to PLN 76.6bn.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
